note: Content per GW, supplier shares and absorption rates are Claude estimates, calibrated so share × content × ~18 GW of global AI capacity a year roughly matches each company’s data center revenue; revenue run-rates are the latest quarter ×4 (Vertiv Q3 $4.31B, GE Vernova Q3 $12.6B; ~ = estimate). Shares that don’t add to 100% go to an “Other suppliers” bucket. Updated with the daily US data center risk task.

cats.why: Supply is capped by CoWoS packaging and HBM, so a delayed US campus mostly frees allocation for other buyers (sovereign AI, Middle East, Asia) rather than cutting shipments.
Head-node and general compute CPUs are less supply-constrained, so lost US racks are only partly re-sold.
Memory is sold out into 2027 at record margins; delayed demand is instantly re-allocated, so the hit shows up as slightly less pricing power, not lower volume.
NAND is tight too, but more exposed to the timing of US storage build-outs.
Ethernet and NVLink switching is bought with each cluster; less absorbed than GPUs because it is designed per site.
EML/CW laser supply is tight (indium phosphide capacity), so part of the demand is absorbed, but transceiver orders follow cluster go-lives closely.
Fiber and cabling are installed on site, so a delayed campus delays the order almost one for one.
Wafers and CoWoS slots are booked a year ahead and re-assigned to other chip customers.
Second derivative: tool orders depend on fab expansion plans, which a 12-month US slip barely moves; test (Teradyne) is closer to unit volumes.

Switchgear, UPS, chillers and liquid cooling are site-specific and ship with construction, so they are the most directly exposed to US delays; 12–18 month backlogs and global customers absorb part of it.
Annual energy sales per GW of load (~8 TWh at ~$65/MWh, the middle of EIA’s $47–85/MWh range for ERCOT North in 2027); a delayed Texas campus is load a Texas generator does not get.

views.NVDA: Largest dollars deferred, smallest real damage: Nvidia is supply-capped, and it is now reportedly financing billions of extra CoWoS capacity at SPIL, which a company expecting a demand cut would not do. A delayed Texas campus mostly hands allocation to Microsoft, sovereign and Asian buyers; Susquehanna puts nearly all permit risk in 2028–2030, so watch hyperscaler capex guides, not state politics.
views.AMD: Exposed through both MI-series GPUs and EPYC CPUs. Its OpenAI (Stargate) ties put more of its 2027 ramp in Texas than peers, so timing risk is above Nvidia's.
views.AVGO: Custom ASIC (Google TPU, Meta, OpenAI) plus Tomahawk switching. Google's $40B Texas plan and Meta's El Paso/Piqua issues touch two of its biggest XPU customers; expect deferrals of quarters, not cancellations.
views.MRVL: Small absolute exposure but high operating leverage; AWS Trainium and optical DSP volumes follow US cluster go-lives closely.
views.ARM: Royalty per CPU is small, so direct impact is negligible; the bigger issue is SoftBank's Stargate financing, which hits sentiment.
views.INTC: Server CPU recovery is tied to general cloud builds more than giant AI campuses, so the hit is modest; foundry ambitions do not depend on US data center siting.
views.SKHY: HBM is sold out; any US slip is re-allocated within weeks. Risk is to the 2027 pricing negotiation, not volume.
views.MU: Same as SK hynix on HBM, with more US-centric enterprise SSD and DRAM module exposure. Pausing the Taoyuan HBM/DRAM fab over a labour dispute trims 2028 supply industry-wide, which supports pricing; Samsung and SK hynix gain qualification time. The Nov 5 drop and partial rebound look like sentiment, not lost orders.
views.SNDK: Datacenter is now 44% of sales and enterprise SSDs ship with each campus, so it carries more timing risk than the HBM makers.
views.COHR: Transceivers and lasers ship close to cluster go-live, so a Texas pause shifts revenue right. But the Nov 4 quarter showed data center revenue up 85% and guidance for 60%+ growth, and the 15% Nov 6 rebound says the market sees the order book outrunning any US delay.
views.LITE: High exposure per dollar of revenue: EML and CW lasers for 800G/1.6T are tied to new clusters. The tight laser market cushions price, not timing.
views.AAOI: Most exposed optics name relative to size; depends on a few hyperscaler programs, some in Texas.
views.GLW: Fiber is installed on site with no absorption, so Corning sees delays almost one for one, but its multi-year hyperscaler contracts (Meta, others) set minimum volumes.
views.TSM: Wafers and CoWoS are booked a year ahead and re-assigned; Nvidia funding outside CoWoS capacity at SPIL shows packaging is still the bottleneck. Effectively immune in 2027 unless global capex falls.
views.AMAT: Second-order only: fab plans for 2027–28 do not change because one US state pauses data centers.
views.ASML: Least exposed; EUV demand is set by memory and logic capacity plans that are still rising.
views.TER: Test volumes follow GPU/HBM unit output, which stays supply-capped, so little impact.
views.VRT: Most directly exposed equipment name: UPS, thermal and liquid cooling ship with construction schedules. Backlog and the shift to friendly states and overseas (Vertiv sells globally) limit lost revenue.
views.ROK: Small AI data center exposure; mostly an industrial cycle story.
views.GEV: Mixed: grid gear for Texas sites slips, but the ratepayer-first rules push hyperscalers to self-supply with gas turbines, which is GE Vernova's sold-out product. Likely net winner.
views.BE: Clear second-order winner: Google's $17B Wyoming campus will run mostly on a 702 MW AEP fuel-cell plant built with Bloom cells, and NTT DATA signed for 900 MW more (deliveries from 2027). Pay-your-own-power rules in the Senate bill and state platforms push hyperscalers to behind-the-meter power that deploys in months, while gas turbines are sold out into the 2030s.
views.VST: Most exposed power name: its growth thesis is new Texas data center load, and management admits the permit pause is already softening ERCOT prices. Still, Q3 beat, 2027 guidance was set above 2026, and it signed a 207 MW Odessa data center PPA, so the 10.6% Nov 6 bounce reflects earnings resilience rather than reduced Texas risk.
views.CEG: Scarcity winner: if new capacity is harder to build, existing nuclear plants with grid hook-ups (PJM, Illinois) become more valuable for hyperscaler deals, though PJM ratepayer politics cap upside.

ownerStack.note: Indicative. Supplier mix per company is Claude’s estimate from public chip, networking and power deals; categories not listed use the industry default mix. Impact = the share of a company’s Building + Blocked GW in hostile states that slips in the next 12 months on the impact map’s base case (delayed GW pro rata, less what is rebuilt in friendly states, moved abroad or switched to on-site power) × content per GW × supplier share × (1 − absorption), i.e. the revenue that would slip if those projects were delayed a year after the supply chain re-sells what it can. Planned GW is shown separately as later-dated. Arm is shown at its royalty (~5% of the CPU value); Grace CPUs count as Nvidia.

msft.chips: Mostly Nvidia GB300/Vera Rubin; some AMD MI and in-house Maia

amzn.chips: Nvidia plus in-house Trainium; Graviton (Arm) CPUs

googl.chips: Mostly TPUs (designed with Broadcom); some Nvidia; Axion (Arm) CPUs

meta.chips: Nvidia, AMD MI-series and MTIA (with Broadcom)

orcl.chips: Nvidia GB200/GB300 for OpenAI Stargate; AMD MI450 cluster

sbank.chips: Nvidia for OpenAI Stargate; OpenAI–Broadcom custom chip later

apld.chips: Nvidia via CoreWeave and hyperscaler tenants

cifr.chips: AWS (Black Pearl) and Fluidstack/Google TPU (Barber Lake)

frmi.chips: All AMD Instinct via TensorWave (lease not yet in effect)
